meta.title: Learning rules, memory dynamics, and biological constraints
meta.subtitle: A claim-evidence map of five years of co-authored work
meta.method_note: Records were derived from the official ISTA author and group publication pages and checked against each paper's abstract. They are literature notes, not author-confirmed Claim Records. Authorship does not by itself identify an individual's precise contribution.

nodes.title: How can neural systems learn under biological constraints?
nodes.claim: Which combinations of synaptic, intrinsic and task-level learning signals can produce useful computation without assuming unrestricted backpropagation?
scope: Learning algorithms in spiking or recurrent network models
Biological plausibility treated as an explicit constraint
non_claims: This question does not imply that one discovered rule is uniquely biological.

nodes.title: How can plastic networks store memories without losing stability?
nodes.claim: How do excitatory-inhibitory codependence, developmental synaptic dynamics and contextual gates control memory formation, stability and accessibility?
non_claims: The papers do not establish one universal memory mechanism.

nodes.title: Which circuit structures support flexible transient computation?
nodes.claim: Which spectral, feedforward, inhibitory and gating structures determine amplification, dimensionality and task-relevant dynamics?
non_claims: A shared theme is not evidence for a single dynamical regime in cortex.

nodes.title: When do cellular constraints become circuit-level causes?
nodes.claim: How do ion-channel kinetics, synaptic transmission, metabolism and developmental state alter neuronal and network function?
non_claims: These studies examine distinct mechanisms and should not be collapsed into one causal chain.

nodes.title: How is flexible behaviour bounded by learned representations?
nodes.claim: How do context, neuromodulation and repertoire constraints trade fidelity against generalisation in memory and vocal behaviour?
non_claims: The two behavioural systems are conceptually related, not evidence for one shared biological mechanism.

nodes.title: The remarkable robustness of surrogate gradient learning for instilling complex function in spiking neural networks
nodes.claim: Across the tested classification problems, surrogate-gradient learning was robust to the derivative's shape but sensitive to its scale; activity regularisation supported information processing at sparse activity levels.
nodes.evidence: Systematic numerical comparison of surrogate-derivative design choices across spiking-network classification tasks.
scope: Published 2021-03-01, before the exact rolling five-year window
Tested numerical tasks and regularisation settings
non_claims: Does not show that surrogate-gradient learning is a biological learning rule.
Does not make derivative shape irrelevant in every architecture or task.

nodes.title: Online learning of neural computations from sparse temporal feedback
nodes.claim: In teacher-student single-neuron models, synaptic and intrinsic parameters were learned online from sparse target-spike feedback using event-based updates without backpropagation through time.
nodes.evidence: Leaky integrate-and-fire and resonate-and-fire teacher-student simulations recovering parameters and temporal input-output functions.
non_claims: Does not establish learning from arbitrary biological feedback.
Does not test a full recurrent circuit.

nodes.title: Predictive learning enables neural networks to learn complex working memory tasks
nodes.authors: Thijs L. Van Der Plas; Tim P. Vogels; Sanjay G. Manohar
nodes.claim: In the tested recurrent-network match tasks, prediction training first created temporal representations and then bootstrapped working-memory performance, with the largest benefit under limited neural resources.
nodes.evidence: Recurrent-network simulations combining prediction objectives with working-memory matching tasks.
non_claims: Does not establish that biological working memory is learned by this mechanism.
The claimed generality is bounded by the tested model tasks.

nodes.title: Balancing complexity, performance and plausibility to meta learn plasticity rules in recurrent spiking networks
nodes.authors: Basile J. Confavreux; Everton J. Agnes; Friedemann Zenke; Henning Sprekeler; Tim P. Vogels
nodes.claim: Evolutionary strategies found local co-active rules that stabilised each of four synapse classes in isolation and could include familiarity detection, while search became difficult as rule complexity and solution degeneracy increased.
nodes.evidence: Meta-learning experiments in large recurrent excitatory-inhibitory spiking networks with increasingly complex plasticity-rule parameterisations.
scope: Four synapse classes tested in isolation
non_claims: Does not identify a unique biological plasticity rule.
Does not solve degeneracy or efficient exploration of complex rule spaces.

nodes.title: Developmental depression-to-facilitation shift controls excitation-inhibition balance
nodes.authors: David W. Jia; Tim P. Vogels; Rui Ponte Costa
nodes.claim: In the model, early excitatory short-term depression buffered strong excitation while slower inhibitory plasticity balanced the network; a developmental shift toward facilitation preserved stability and changed temporal responses.
nodes.evidence: Computational models of developmental short-term synaptic dynamics coupled to inhibitory long-term plasticity.
non_claims: Does not experimentally establish this shift as the developmental cause of E/I balance.

nodes.title: Co-dependent excitatory and inhibitory plasticity accounts for quick, stable and long-lasting memories in biological networks
nodes.authors: Everton J. Agnes; Tim P. Vogels
nodes.claim: A formal model of synaptic codependence reproduced rapid and stable weight profiles and generated input-sensitive, motor-cortex-like recurrent dynamics by coupling excitatory and inhibitory plasticity.
nodes.evidence: Analytical framework and simulations spanning synaptic profiles, dendritic clustering and recurrent-network dynamics.
scope: Modelled orientation, dendritic and recurrent-network phenomena
non_claims: Does not establish that the same codependence rule operates in every biological network.
Motor-cortex-like dynamics are model consistency, not direct biological validation.

nodes.title: High capacity and dynamic accessibility in associative memory networks with context-dependent neuronal and synaptic gating
nodes.authors: William F. Podlaski; Everton J. Agnes; Tim P. Vogels
nodes.claim: In context-modular associative-memory models, neuronal or synaptic gating reduced cross-context interference, improving capacity and permitting context-specific control of memory stability and accessibility.
nodes.evidence: Analytical and numerical results for random gating and optimised contextual synaptic refinement.
non_claims: Does not show that biological memory uses the proposed gating scheme.
Capacity and accessibility trade-offs are model-specific quantities.

nodes.title: Noradrenaline causes a spread of association in the hippocampal cognitive map
nodes.authors: Renee S. Koolschijn et al., including Tim P. Vogels
nodes.claim: A human pharmacological intervention and neural-network model linked elevated noradrenaline during learning to broader associations across a hippocampal cognitive map and behavioural overgeneralisation.
nodes.evidence: Cross-scale human pharmacology, neural measurements and modelling of plasticity smoothing.
scope: Model-based interpretation of a plasticity smoothing kernel
non_claims: Does not imply that noradrenaline always improves or impairs memory.
The model is an explanation of the observed spread, not a unique mechanism.

nodes.title: Regimes and mechanisms of transient amplification in abstract and biological neural networks
nodes.authors: Georgia Christodoulou; Tim P. Vogels; Everton J. Agnes
nodes.claim: Separating eigenspectrum from feedforward structure with a Schur-basis construction revealed a trade-off between amplification and trajectory dimensionality; in Dale-constrained networks, global inhibition tracked amplification strength.
nodes.evidence: Analytical and numerical manipulation of linear, nonlinear and excitatory-inhibitory network models.
scope: Constructed abstract and biological network models
non_claims: Does not establish global inhibition as the unique controller of amplification in vivo.

nodes.title: Developmentally regulated impairment of parvalbumin interneuron synaptic transmission in an experimental model of Dravet syndrome
nodes.authors: Keisuke Kaneko et al., including Tim P. Vogels
nodes.claim: In Scn1a+/- mice, early PV-interneuron spike-generation impairment normalised in survivors, while synaptic-transmission dysfunction persisted; modelling indicated axonal propagation was more sensitive to reduced sodium conductance.
nodes.evidence: Longitudinal mouse electrophysiology paired with computational modelling of spike generation and axonal propagation.
non_claims: Does not show identical disease dynamics in every Dravet genotype or in humans.

nodes.title: Metabolically regulated spiking could serve neuronal energy homeostasis and protect from reactive oxygen species
nodes.claim: Models showed that self-initiated spiking could act as a metabolic release valve under low energy use, reproduce ROS-linked intrinsic-firing changes, and sustain avalanche-like cortical dynamics.
nodes.evidence: Models integrating ATP, ADP and ROS homeostasis with firing, including a fruit-fly neuron model and cortical-circuit simulations.
non_claims: Does not experimentally demonstrate that spontaneous firing serves this purpose.
The broad homeostasis interpretation remains a hypothesis with explicit predictions.

nodes.title: A structurally precise mechanism links an epilepsy-associated KCNC2 potassium channel mutation to interneuron dysfunction
nodes.authors: Jerome Clatot et al., including Tim P. Vogels
nodes.claim: Experiments and molecular simulations identified a gain-of-function effect of Kv3.2-Cys125Tyr, while a multicompartment PV-interneuron model linked the altered channel kinetics to reduced excitability and dysregulated cortical inhibition.
nodes.evidence: Patient variant identification, channel electrophysiology, molecular dynamics and multicompartment neuronal modelling.
non_claims: Does not generalise the mechanism to all KCNC2 variants or epilepsies.

nodes.title: Mitochondrial Ca2+ efflux controls neuronal metabolism and long-term memory across species
nodes.authors: Anjali Amrapali Vishwanath et al., including Tim P. Vogels
nodes.claim: Reducing Letm1-mediated mitochondrial calcium efflux increased neuronal mitochondrial metabolism and enhanced long-term-memory storage in fly and mouse paradigms where controls failed to remember.
nodes.evidence: Cross-species genetic and physiological interventions in central memory circuits, with behavioural long-term-memory assays.
scope: Tested training paradigms and central memory circuits
non_claims: Does not imply that globally increasing neuronal metabolism is uniformly beneficial or safe.

nodes.title: Cortical development dynamics across autism spectrum disorder mouse models
nodes.authors: Lena A. Schwarz et al., including Tim P. Vogels
nodes.claim: Across 11 monogenic ASD mouse models, multi-omic profiles converged on transient radial-glial developmental delays and stage-specific neuronal changes, while genotype-specific and sex-specific heterogeneity remained.
nodes.evidence: 251 single-nucleus multi-omic samples across development, sexes and brain regions, supported by electrophysiology.
non_claims: Does not define one permanent ASD cell state.
Mouse-model convergence does not erase genotype, sex or human heterogeneity.

nodes.title: Interplay between syllable duration and pitch during whistle matching in wild nightingales
nodes.authors: Juan Sebastian Calderon Garcia; Giacomo Costalunga; Tim P. Vogels; Daniela Vallentin
nodes.claim: Playback experiments and a computational model indicated that nightingales trade pitch matching against duration imitation, with syllable duration providing a temporal constraint and the natural repertoire limiting responses.
nodes.evidence: Wild-bird playback experiments using natural and unnatural pitch-duration combinations, paired with a hierarchical feature-production model.
non_claims: Does not establish the same feature hierarchy in other vocal learners.

nodes.title: Learning rules become objects of search, not fixed assumptions
nodes.claim: Across the mapped modelling papers, the programme moves from testing robust optimisation surrogates and sparse feedback toward explicitly searching local plasticity-rule families under performance and plausibility constraints.
non_claims: This is not a claim made or validated by one paper.
The mapped work does not identify a unique biological rule.

nodes.title: Memory flexibility repeatedly appears as a controlled trade-off
nodes.claim: Across distinct models and experiments, stability, accessibility, fidelity and generalisation are traded through synaptic codependence, contextual gating or neuromodulatory broadening of plasticity.
non_claims: Gating and noradrenergic smoothing are not shown to be the same mechanism.

nodes.title: Cellular constraints are treated as computational variables
nodes.claim: The mapped collaborations connect channel kinetics, synaptic propagation, metabolism and developmental state to circuit or behavioural outcomes using combinations of mechanistic models and experiments.
scope: Methodological synthesis across separate biological mechanisms
non_claims: The studies do not form one continuous causal pathway.
Precise individual author contributions were not inferred.

nodes.title: Modelling is increasingly paired with behavioural intervention
nodes.claim: The 2026 behavioural papers use models to express bounded trade-offs exposed by intervention: association spread after pharmacology and pitch-duration trade-offs after playback.
non_claims: Does not imply a common neural implementation across humans and birds.
